questions.q: What happens when you write max_tokens = 500 in Python?
options: 500 is treated as text because it has no explicit type
You must write int max_tokens = 500 instead
Python creates the variable and infers it's an int, with no separate declaration step needed
Python raises an error because the type wasn't declared first
questions.explain: Python is dynamically typed — assignment alone creates the variable and infers its type from the value.

questions.q: What makes None different from 0, an empty string, or False?
options: None is just another way to write 0
None explicitly means 'no value has been set,' distinct from any of those real values
None only exists in other languages, not Python
None and False are always interchangeable in Python
questions.explain: None represents the explicit absence of a value — it's a different concept from 0, "", or False, which are all real values.

questions.q: What does type(temperature) return if temperature = 0.7?
options: <class 'bool'>
<class 'int'>
<class 'str'>
<class 'float'>
questions.explain: 0.7 has a decimal point, so Python assigns it the float type.

questions.q: What happens if you try to run "5" + 3 in Python?
options: It returns the number 8
It raises a TypeError, since Python won't silently combine a string and an int
It automatically converts both to floats and adds them
It returns the string "53"
questions.explain: Unlike some languages, Python raises a TypeError rather than silently coercing types — you must convert explicitly with int() or str().

questions.q: What does an f-string let you do?
options: Force a variable to always be a float
Declare a variable's type explicitly before assigning it
Run a file without using the python command
Embed variables directly inside a text string using curly braces, after putting f before the opening quote
questions.explain: f"text {variable}" is the standard way to build text that includes variable values.
